researcher: Claude (web research session); sources opened and read for the cited facts
thesis: Costco's prices can stay low because the membership card, not the merchandise, carries about half of the company's operating profit.

contradictions.note: Search summaries put membership fees at $5,323 million, but the opened press-release table showed a quarterly $1,724 million. Resolution: FY2025 membership fees are DERIVED from the same primary table as total revenue ($275,235M) minus net sales ($269,912M) = $5,323M, which matches the figure other summaries reported.

sources.title: Q4 and fiscal year 2025 results (8-K exhibit 99.1)
Form 10-K for fiscal year ended August 31, 2025
Why Costco hot dogs have kept $1.50 price tag since 1985
sources.use: context only; single secondary source, hot dog claims are NOT used in the script

claims.text: Costco's fiscal 2025 total revenue was $275,235 million against net sales of $269,912 million; the difference, membership fees, was $5,323 million (about $5.3 billion).
Costco's fiscal 2025 operating income was $10,383 million (about $10.4 billion), so membership fees equal roughly 51% of operating income.
The 10-K says Costco does not focus in the short term on maximizing prices charged, and instead seeks a perception among members of 'pricing authority'.
Costco's renewal rate was 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide at the end of fiscal 2025, with about 81.0 million paid members.

inferences.text: Membership fees of $5.3 billion divided by operating income of $10.4 billion is about 51%.

angle: Costco sells the discount, and the card is the product. Only primary-source numbers; hot-dog folklore deliberately left out because only one secondary source was verified.
